motion.name: turbine
motion.purpose: One restrained ambient movement, paused with driving and under reduced motion

experienceFidelity.behavior: Inertial driving now turns all wheel/hub geometry and banks/pitches the service rover. A bounded pursuit camera follows its physical position and eases into a slightly closer view at speed. Destination selection frames the landmark instead of relocating the rover; closing reverses to its real position. Rendering is capped at 30fps and sun shadow texture at 1024px. The enamel route log remains unchanged.
experienceFidelity.limits: Kinematic keep-out boxes, not rigid-body vehicle physics; no source-level physics toys, weather or reflections. Coast rendering measured only 2 desktop / 4 phone renders per second under this heavily concurrent software-WebGL run. This is not a smoothness pass. Initial 2.5-second paused snapshots had 1/2 residual camera frames; the diagnostic confirmed zero work after settling, but settling took ~15 seconds in this environment. One inherited hover contrast advisory is 4.46:1 vs 4.5:1; it remains unresolved. Tinted offset shadow warnings are retained accepted elevation, not newly added effects.

components.name: Destination sign
components.description: A clickable label attached to a world landmark

narrative.overview: A materially lit miniature industrial coastline, not a 3D chart. Architecture has roof seams, glazing, pipes, loading awnings, visible server racks, cables and pier planks. Visitors explore with an original six-wheel utility rover; the surrounding page is a restrained field guide.
keyCharacteristics: Golden sandstone and orange enamel against a deep coastal ground.
Detailed original procedural geometry, physical cast shadows and quiet signage.
Information remains independent of game skill.
dos: Do retain direct access to all professional information.
Do keep the original world coherent in architecture, material and light.
donts: Don't treat illustrative scenery as evidence of actual client projects or infrastructure.
Don't substitute abstract primitive diagrams for the detailed landscape.
Don't imply mechanical browser passes establish reference-level visual acceptance.
